name: MI-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+9 PVI) in a favorable environment
Jeremy Moss's large fundraising edge over Ethan Baker
Prediction markets price Democrats near 96% to hold the seat
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot adds some uncertainty
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Democrats: a D+9 district, a favorable national environment, and Moss outraising Baker roughly ten-to-one with outside support on his side. Markets price a Democratic hold at about 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unusually strong GOP year in metro Detroit could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Haley Stevens is leaving this Detroit-area seat to run for Senate, making MI-11 an open contest. State Senator Jeremy Moss enters as the clear Democratic favorite, backed by a district that voted about nine points Democratic in recent baselines and a national environment that has leaned toward his party. He has raised nearly $1.5 million and holds a large cash advantage over Republican Ethan Baker, a county commissioner who has raised under $150,000.

Independent and minor-party candidates, including well-funded independent Anil Kumar, could siphon some votes, but none appear positioned to threaten the two-party outcome. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat, and the fundamentals support that view. The race is rated Safe D, with the main caveat being the absence of an incumbent and any public polling.
